Subject: RE: OryxAI capacity ask: surge hedge, latency targets, and fallback ops

Kim / Priyom / Ethan —

Preliminary sizing notes (assumptions called out):
- Assumed production model: rwd-13b quantized (int8) for main path; fallback: rwd-7b-int8.
- Avg generated tokens per request: 80; average latency budget target for runtime-only (infra + model exec) = 180 ms (leaves ~70 ms for network + client).
- Target p95 end-to-end: <= 250 ms -> runtime p95 target ~180 ms.

Base perf estimates (empirical from similar customers on H100 80GB slab):
- rwd-13b-int8: ~0.9 ms / token single-request per-GPU throughput for small batch steady-state; effective per-GPU sustained token output ~1,100 tokens/sec when preserving p95<=180ms with continuous batching (workload dependent).
- rwd-7b-int8: ~0.45 ms / token; effective per-GPU sustained token output ~2,200 tokens/sec.

Sizing math (steady-state):
- Required sustained GPUs for 45k t/s with rwd-13b-int8 = ceil(45,000 / 1,100) = 41 GPUs (logical serving slots).
- With typical slab packing (ten 4-GPU nodes per slab) that's ~11 slabs of H100-80GB (round up to 12 slabs to avoid fragmentation).

Burst headroom (recommendation):
- We recommend 40% headroom on top of steady-state to cover traffic spikes and KV-cache warmup. That maps to provisioning target = 45k * 1.4 = 63k tokens/sec -> 63k / 1,100 ~= 58 GPUs -> ~15 slabs.
- For extreme short flash events (160k t/s), full provision would require ~145 GPUs (not economical as reserved). Instead we recommend a hybrid: reserved capacity sized to 40% headroom + autoscale burst pool + deterministic fallback.

Fallback / graceful degradation options (ordered):
1) Route to rwd-7b-int8 (lower quality) with significantly higher per-GPU throughput (~2,200 t/s), reduces GPU needs by ~2.0x for bursts.
2) Shorten generation length via token cap policy (e.g., cap at 64 tokens for non-critical requests) + early-exit heuristics.
3) Queueing + prioritized tiers (paying users vs free tiers) with deterministic 503s for lowest tier.

Operational implications / SLA bullets:
- Canary plan: start with 6 slabs (24 GPUs) reserved, validate traffic shaping and cache-warm paths, then scale to 12 slabs as usage stabilizes.
- Autoscale: aggressive burst pool backed by cloud spot capacity for ephemeral surges; we recommend pre-authorized burst budget in the contract.

Attachments: oryx_compute_sizing.xlsx (detailed per-model worksheet), gpu_slab_diagram.png (logical slab packing).

Open questions for Ethan:
- Confirm model family and tolerance for quantized variant (accuracy delta targets).
- Clarify peak flash duration distribution (30–90s in your note is helpful; any monthly frequency estimate?).

If those items look good, I'll convert these into a simple capacity + pricing table for Kimberly to include in the SLA draft.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ethan —

Great — we can do that. Summary / commitments from Redwood (actionable deliverables):

1) Sizing + pricing deliverables (by 2026-10-26):
  - Two provisioning scenarios with per-month committed pricing and burst/overage rates:
    a) Conservative reserved: 12 slabs (H100-80GB), covers ~63k t/s (recommended steady+40% headroom).
    b) Staged reserved + burst: 6 slabs reserved + pre-authorized burst pool (cloud-backed) for short events.
  - Each scenario will include a blended 12-month cost estimate and an estimated effective $/1k tokens for steady vs burst usage.

2) SLA text (draft) + remedies (by 2026-10-26):
  - Runtime p95 target: <= 180 ms (runtime-only). End-to-end p95 target in SLA: <= 250 ms.
  - Credit: If monthly end-to-end p95 > 250 ms for >1 contiguous hour, customer receives service credit equal to 5% of that months committed fee per hour over threshold, up to 50% (draft language). We will iterate with legal.

3) Overage & burst runbook (by 2026-10-26):
  - Flash bursts (<2 min): billed at dynamic burst rate, with a pre-burn budget for first 10 minutes per event if pre-authorized.
  - Cache warmup guidance: typical KV/prefix cache warmup to steady efficiency ~45–90s depending on session affinity; we'll include warmup tuning options (pre-warming endpoints for launches).

4) Compliance artifacts: SOC2 report summary, KMS integration options, audit log sample export, and data retention policy - we will attach redacted artifacts and list options for Private deployment.

Operational recommendation (short):
- Start with staged reserved + burst (6 slabs reserved) for 30-day pilot. Run canary at 25% traffic to validate latency profile and cache behavior, then expand to 12 slabs if the predicted token velocity is realized.
- Implement automatic model-swap rule: when per-second inbound tokens > reserved capacity * 1.1 for >45s, route non-critical traffic to rwd-7b-int8 and throttle the rest. That gives deterministic quality/latency tradeoffs.

I'll assemble the above into the SLA + pricing packet and share a link to the HubSpot deal and sample DocuSign for your procurement team. If Friday 10/22 works for a 30-min call, Ben and Priyom can present the sizing and runbook; otherwise we can keep this in email.

Thanks — we'll be in touch with the deliverables this week.

—Kimberly
